title: Cap. 7 Theologi nostri: Zanchius — sufficiently for all, efficaciously for elect
pass_a_gloss: Zanchi, in the Miscellanies, treatise On the Predestination of the Saints, page 14. It is not false that Christ died for all men: for to all the passion of Christ is offered in the Gospel. But he died efficaciously only for the elect: because namely they alone become partakers of the efficacy of Christ's passion. But that they alone become partakers of this passion efficaciously is to be referred to the special and efficacious will of Christ suffering, and of God the Father accepting this victim, for the elect in a more peculiar manner than for others. For in the participation of saving good the Divine will precedes the human.
pass_b_english: Zanchi (Miscellanies, On the Predestination of the Saints, p. 14): it is not false that Christ died for all men — his passion is offered to all in the Gospel. Yet he died efficaciously only for the elect, because they alone share the passion's efficacy. That they alone so share it must be referred to the special, effectual will of Christ suffering and of the Father accepting this victim — for the elect in a more peculiar way than for others. In sharing saving good, the divine will goes before the human.
source_text: Zanchius, in Miscellaneis, tract. De praedest. san. pag. 14. Falsum non est, Christum mortuum pro omnibus hominibus: Omnibus enim passio Christi offertur in Evangelio. Sed pro electis tantum efficaciter mortuus est: quia scilicet ipsi tantum efficacitatis passionis Christi participes fiunt. Quod autem illi soli fiant participes hujus passionis efficaciter, id referendum est ad specialem & efficacem voluntatem Christi patientis, Deique Patris hanc hostiam acceptantis, pro electis magis peculiari modo quam pro aliis. In boni enim salutiferi participatione voluntas Divina praecedit humanam.
